touristAppeal.label: Notable Stop
touristAppeal.summary: Cellardyke now supports a substantial half-day visit: a restored tidal pool, bookable sauna and outdoor activities reinforce an unusually coherent fishing-burgh harbour, interpreted lanes, local food and two real walking routes.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: The harbour, historic streets and coast path work well with a controlled dog, but dog policies are not published for the pool, sauna, activity centre or gallery and indoor food access is limited or unconfirmed.

visitorHighlights.name: Cellardyke Tidal Pool
visitorHighlights.reason: A restored and genuinely usable sea pool with a strong coastal setting, practical companion facilities and an active community programme.
visitorHighlights.tagline: Restored Isle of May sea pool
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Open-air site. Check tide, swell and weather; high or rough water can make the hardstanding unsafe.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A distinctive restored sea-bathing experience with strong presentation and companion facilities, reduced for weather dependence and physical access constraints.

visitorHighlights.name: East Neuk Outdoors
visitorHighlights.reason: A broad, bookable activity offer backed by a current Adventure Activities Licence and qualified instruction.
visitorHighlights.timeToSpend: From a come-and-try session to a full day
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Pre-booked sessions; programme varies by date and conditions.
visitorHighlights.admission: Paid activity sessions; individual prices are shown on the live booking page.
visitorHighlights.sourceName: East Neuk Outdoors and HSE AALA

editorialReview.scoreRationale: Strong activity depth, qualified delivery and bookable reliability; reduced because sessions need advance planning and the mapped point is postcode-representative.

visitorHighlights.name: Cellardyke Harbour (Skinfast Haven)
visitorHighlights.reason: A compact and unusually coherent historic fishing harbour with community interpretation woven into the surrounding townscape.
visitorHighlights.tagline: Skinfast Haven and the black dykes
visitorHighlights.sourceName: Fife Council and Cellardyke historical boards

editorialReview.scoreRationale: Strong townscape distinctiveness and historical interpretation, reduced because it is a small working open-air harbour rather than a managed attraction.

visitorHighlights.name: Cellardyke Seaside Sauna
visitorHighlights.reason: A polished, bookable wood-fired sauna experience directly paired with the restored tidal pool and open sea view.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A distinctive and well-presented bookable experience with transparent price and capacity, reduced for limited parking, lack of changing facilities and narrow audience.

visitorHighlights.name: Cellardyke Historic Streets and Boards
visitorHighlights.reason: Six physical boards and deeper online stories turn the historic lanes into a coherent self-guided fishing-burgh experience.
visitorHighlights.sourceName: Cellardyke historical boards and Fife Council

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A genuine interpreted townscape walk with distinctive local material, but modest infrastructure and no formal downloadable route.

visitorHighlights.name: Gallery 495
visitorHighlights.reason: A changing contemporary-art programme gives the harbour phone box a tiny but memorable second life.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Visible from the public realm; check the current programme online.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: Very distinctive and current, but necessarily a micro-attraction with little visit depth.

townGuide.characterTag: Fishing burgh, sea pool and active coast
townGuide.headline: A working harbour village with a restored bathing culture
townGuide.intro: Cellardyke is more than Anstruther’s eastern edge. Its tiny Skinfast Haven, black dykes and close-built lanes tell the fishing-burgh story, while the restored tidal pool, seaside sauna and East Neuk Outdoors make the eastern shore an active visitor hub.
perfectFor: A substantial half-day East Neuk visit
Visitors combining heritage with an outdoor activity

suggestedFirstVisit.title: Start at Skinfast Haven and walk east
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Read the harbour boards and Gallery 495, follow the historic lanes towards Toon’s Green, then finish at the tidal pool, sauna and The Grind.

townGuide.suggestedTime: 3–5 hours; longer with a booked activity or the Crail coastal-path stage
townGuide.visitorMood: A notably complete small coastal stop: intimate rather than grand, but with enough real experiences, food and walking to justify planning several hours.

features.fullDescription: 1878; extended 1896. 2-storey, 7-bay, T-plan Board school with gothic porches. Squared rubble with squared snecking and stugged ashlar dressings. Base, band and 1st floor cill courses, and eaves cornice. Hoodmoulded Tudor-arch doors, and shouldered windows. Stop-chamfered arrises and stone mullions. S (ENTRANCE) ELEVATION: symmetrical. Low wall projecting to centre at ground, flanking bays each with raised centre tripartite window and gothic porch beyond in re-entrant angle with tiny blind niche in steeply-pitched gablehead, timber door and narrow light to inner return at ground; centre bay at 1st floor with relief carved panel worded 'ERECTED 1878/ENLARGED 1896' surmounted by scrolled broken pediment and 2 closely aligned bipartite windows to flanking bays. M-gables to advanced outer bays each with raised centre tripartite window to ground and 1st floor (latter slightly wider), and timber-louvered opening in gablehead. E ELEVATION: 2 raised centre tripartite windows to ground and 2 further tripartite windows to 1st floor. N (REAR) ELEVATION: symmetrical elevation with largely regular fenestration, 2 advanced piend-roofed bays to centre and further piend-roofed outer bays. Later flat-roofed single storey projections to right and left of centre. W ELEVATION: as E elevation. Horizontal 3- and 4-pane glazing patterns to ground and 1st floor E, 6-, 8- and 10-pane glazing patterns elsewhere, all in timber sash and case windows. Grey slates. Ashlar-coped skews with flat skewputts. Cast-iron downpipes with decorative rainwater hoppers and fixings, and square-section gutters.

Few loft hatches to E elevation extant, that to No 3 remains. Variety of glazing, some 6-pane fixed lights. Some simple timber boarded doors. Some ridge stacks remain. features.fullDescription: The Cardinal Steps bathing pool was created by local improvement fundraising in the 1930s and revived through a community-led restoration campaign.
